title: Restricted K-injective coefficient systems are acyclic for ordinary inverse limit
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and an arbitrary scheme W. Use the actual coefficient sequence site and restriction U = coefficientSequenceRestriction of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site], and its complex functor tower [def-trf-completion-unit-models]. For every K-injective coefficient-system complex I, every K-injective complex J of towers of completed-coefficient modules, and every quasi-isomorphism j : tower(I) -> J, the degreewise ordinary inverse-limit map lim(j) is a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction itself is not asserted to preserve K-injectivity. There is no invertibility-of-l, boundedness, or flatness hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the vertical-slice equivalence between modules on the coefficient sequence site and strict semilinear systems. Its exactness preserves K-injectivity. Identify the specified restriction with the strict-system restrictionFunctor by its unique object, horizontal-map and morphism characterizations; this yields an isomorphism of restricted tower complexes, natural in I.

Transport j through that isomorphism. Apply the first conclusion of acyclicity from lem-coef-restricted-tower-resolution-acyclicity with the identity system resolution. It says that ordinary lim sends this tower resolution to a quasi-isomorphism. Conjugating by the degreewise limit of the transport isomorphism gives the claimed map lim(j). No K-injectivity of the restricted tower is used.

theorem restricted_limit_acyclic
    (I : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E W) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (J : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) ℤ) [J.IsKInjective]
    (j : (tower l E W).obj I ⟶ J) [QuasiIso j] :
    QuasiIso (((lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource l E W) ⥤
      scalarReductionSource l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map j)
